name: JM Financial Ltd
title: JM Financial Ltd-$ - 523405 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 PAT ex-provisions after minority was flat at INR302 crores; Private Markets revenue doubled to INR462 crores on lumpy ARC resolutions while Capital Markets revenue fell to INR115 crores from INR182 crores.

summary.headline: JM Financial Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 13% YoY to INR883 crores, with Private Markets doubling to INR462 crores offsetting weak capital markets.
summary.overview: Consolidated net revenue grew 13% YoY to INR883 crores and pre-provision operating profit rose 21% to INR469 crores. PAT ex-provisions before minorities rose 24% to INR379 crores, but after minorities it was flat at INR302 crores; reported PAT was INR292 crores (annualised ROE about 11%). Private Markets, led by a large distressed-credit resolution, carried the quarter while Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets and Wealth were weak on lack of primary issuance. Management said July revenues on the transaction side already exceeded June.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated net worth / book value per share

segments.name: Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR115 crores vs INR182 crores a year ago; PAT INR32 crores. Closed 9 capital markets transactions worth about INR22,000 crores; filed for 60 IPOs aggregating about INR150,000 crores, excluding Jio Platforms and NSE.

segments.name: Wealth Management
segments.commentary: Net revenue INR185 crores vs INR211 crores; PAT INR19 crores. Wealth loan book up 43% YoY to INR2,417 crores; recurring AUM about INR33,400 crores, now 30% of total AUM; 1,000+ RMs, 71 branches.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: Mutual fund management fees up 62% YoY to INR13 crores; loss after minorities flat at INR5 crores. Non-liquid AUM about INR10,900 crores, up 16% QoQ; employees up 10% YoY to 222.

segments.name: Private Markets
segments.commentary: Net revenue doubled YoY to INR462 crores; pre-provision operating profit about 2.3x to INR375 crores; segment PAT after minorities INR228 crores. Gross ARC resolutions over INR2,000 crores, group share of cash flows over INR1,200 crores.

segments.name: Affordable Home Loans
segments.commentary: AUM up 28% YoY to INR3,715 crores; disbursements up 87% YoY; revenue up 22% to INR123 crores; PAT after minorities up 16% to INR17 crores. 151 branches, about 36,000 customers.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Private Markets to meet its guidance; bespoke credit book targeted to grow 15-20% YoY, with about half of that already achieved in Q1.
Capital markets pipeline of about INR150,000 crores excluding Jio and NSE; management hopes to execute a majority of it in the rest of FY27.
Net flows in Wealth expected at minimum about INR6,000 crores for the year vs about INR2,000 crores in Q1.
ROE for FY27 guided in a similar range to last year (about 11.5%) or better; management aims to push Wealth and Asset Management ROE into the mid-to-high teens over time.
Asset Management to get INR150 crores further investment over next 2 years; management targets AMC AUM of INR25,000 crores.
Debt-to-equity expected to rise from 0.8x to about 2x within 3 years as syndication ramps; ARC expected to become debt-free within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Affordable Home Loans: 151 branches; plan to list the business separately in 2 to 3 years.
Asset Management: INR150 crores further investment over next 2 years.
Wealth: recruitment of 100+ RMs over last 18 months; 2 to 3 year profitability gestation; 5-year plan approved by Board last year.
ARC distressed credit book INR3,114 crores at Q1 (down from INR3,665 crores in Q4 FY26) after about INR1,200 crores recovery and INR600 crores new deployment.
demand_pricing: ARC returns: wholesale 18-22% IRR, retail 15-18%; new-book ARC transactions show IRRs of 18%+ and blended 16-18%.
Equity allocation INR970 crores (flat for 5 quarters); alternatives allocation about INR500 crores vs INR300 crores earlier; cash about INR3,000 crores earning about 6%.
Margin trade financing book about INR2,500 crores with combined yield about 13.5%; management sees 15% annual growth.
Credit syndication income about INR20 crores in Q1.
Industry wealth AUM growth expected at early to mid-teens; management targets above-industry growth.
Mutual fund equity AUM about INR10,500 crores, up from under INR500 crores three years ago; SIP book down about 30% per analyst question, management expects stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cyclicality break in wealth and private credit, and when does organic credit growth start?
qa_highlights.answer: Bespoke book reached about INR3,000 crores, a 5-quarter high, and is about halfway to the 15-20% annual growth guided in Q4. Wealth is a 2-3 year build-out, with FY27 and FY28 expected to be productivity-led.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wealth profitability drop sharply, and will employee costs as a share of revenue fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower transactional revenue and gestation of 100+ RMs hired in 18 months, who take 2.5-3 years to turn profitable. Management said headcount has likely peaked, with hiring now selective.

qa_highlights.question: Asset management SIP book down about 30% and AUM flat; what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-liquid AUM rose 16% QoQ; decline was linked to small/mid-cap concentration. Management engaged more distributors and expects SIP and AUM to recover over the next couple of quarters. Quantitative targets to be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state ROE is achievable excluding market peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ROE was about 11.5%, constrained by the 50% NBFC payout cap. Management expects a similar or better range this year, with stronger ROE from Wealth and AMC operating leverage in about 2 years; CACM is about 15% ROE in a weak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Private Markets carries 60-65% of capital and drags ROE; will capital mix change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-to-equity is at a low of 0.8x and will rise toward 2x in about 3 years as syndication grows, lifting ROE into the teens. Dividends constrained to 50% of NBFC profits.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q1 Private Markets revenue came from the single large ARC transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARC income is lumpy and largely booked on resolution; the June quarter included a big resolution, while book value fell by about INR1,200 crores of recovery and about INR600 crores was redeployed.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for demerger or listing of wealth and asset management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wealth and AM are still small; it will evaluate a listing or demerger at scale, subject to no tax leakage. Affordable housing listing is planned in 2-3 years.

risks_watch: Capital markets recovery: July transaction revenue reportedly above June, but the INR150,000 crore IPO pipeline (ex-Jio and NSE) depends on FDI flows staying net buyers and on primary issuance resuming.
Private Markets lumpiness: ARC income is booked largely on resolution, so Q1 was flattered by one large resolution; 2-3 large pre-COVID resolutions and real estate write-backs are still pending.
Wealth profitability: PAT fell to INR19 crores as 100+ RMs hired over 18 months mature (2.5-3 years to profitability); watch employee cost ratio and productivity.
Asset Management: SIP book reportedly down about 30%, linked to small/mid-cap concentration; management promised quantitative targets separately, which are not yet disclosed.

ROE drag: Private Markets carries about 60-65% of capital, NBFC dividend payout capped at 50% of profit, and debt-to-equity fell to 0.8x; the plan to lift leverage to about 2x within 3 years depends on syndication ramping.
Ex-provision PAT after minorities was flat at INR302 crores, so the 24% growth before minorities does not fully reach shareholders; monitor the minority share.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 results demonstrate the strength of our diversified business model, and pleased to report that the Private Markets segment provided very strong cushion to the earnings amidst volatility in Capital Markets.
The month of July, our revenues on the transaction side in Corporate Advisory and Capital Markets for the month of July already exceed what we have done in June, which is a very, very positive sign.
So I think it's just about continuing to focus on the execution, and fairly confident at some point in time we'll see very, very encouraging sort of stats and numbers on the wealth business, as said.
Yes, we can provide them separately.
I would imagine that our current debt equity, which has reached 0.8x, I think we are almost at the lowest.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Private Markets and ARC returns and on early July capital markets recovery, but cautious on Wealth and Asset Management, where management conceded weak transaction revenue and SIP decline. Evasive on quantitative Asset Management targets (to be shared separately) and on the timing of the Wealth profitability turnaround, which it tied to a 2-3 year build-out.
